title: C# Multiple Choice Questions - Namespaces
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on namespaces in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a namespace in the .NET Framework Class Library?
questions.explanation: System.Process is not a namespace (Process lives in System.Diagnostics). System.Security, System.Threading, and System.Xml are BCL namespaces.

questions.question: Which is the correct statement about the namespaces in C#.NET?

options.text: Nesting of namespaces is permitted, provided all the inner namespaces are declared in the same file
There is no limit on the number of levels while nesting namespaces

questions.question: Which among the following does not belong to the C#.NET namespace?
Which among the following is a correct statement about namespace used in C#.NET?

options.text: Classes must belong to a namespace, whereas structures need not
All elements of the namespace must to belong to one file
If a namespace is not specified, types are placed in the global namespace

questions.explanation: C# does not invent a namespace from the project name. Types declared outside any namespace go in the global namespace. Classes and structs follow the same rule, and a namespace may span multiple files.

questions.question: Which among the given is not a correct way to call the method issue() defined in the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation: Book lives in College.Lib. A fully qualified name or a using College.Lib; directive is required. Book b = new Book(); without importing that namespace does not compile.

questions.question: Which among the following statements are not correct about a namespace used in C#.NET?

options.text: Importing outer namespaces imports inner namespace
Importing outer namespace does not import inner namespace

questions.question: Which among the following is a .NET namespace?
If a class named csharp is present in namespace n1 as well as in namespace n2, then which of the following is the correct way to use csharp class?
questions.explanation: When the same type name exists in two namespaces, use fully qualified names (n1.csharp / n2.csharp) or using aliases. using directives cannot appear inside a method, and import is Java, not C#.

questions.question: If ListBox is the class of System.Windows.Forms namespace. Then, the correct way to create an object of ListBox class is?

options.text:
using System.Windows.Forms;
ListBox I = new ListBox();

using LBControl = System.Windows.Forms.ListBox;
LBControl I = new LBControl();

questions.explanation: You may import the namespace, use a fully qualified name, or introduce a using alias for the type (using Alias = Namespace.Type;).

questions.question: Which among the following is the correct statement about the using statement used in C#.NET?

options.text: A C#.NET source code file consists of any number of using statement
By using 'using' statement it's possible to create an alias for the namespace but not for the namespace element
It is permitted to define a member at namespace level using alias
Using statement can be placed anywhere in the C#.NET source code file

questions.explanation: A file may contain any number of using directives. They belong at compilation-unit or namespace level, not inside methods. A using alias may name a namespace or a type; it does not define a namespace member.
